# STL fixtures

Generated by `python3 tools/cad-fixtures/generate-stl-fixtures.py` using Python's
standard library. `manifest.json` records hashes, byte counts, nominal source-unit
dimensions/volumes, encoding, and expected production solid-validation result.
The fixtures are original project geometry dedicated to CC0; see `LICENSE.txt`.
The generator remains under the repository source-code license.

- Cubes: ASCII and binary, one source unit per edge. The binary header starts
  with `solid` deliberately. Stored normals are zero: winding defines normals.
- Cylinders: radius 0.5, height 1; 16/32/64 planar sides. Polygon volume is
  `n * 0.125 * sin(2*pi/n)`, not the exact cylinder volume. Coordinates are
  quantized to binary32 before either encoding; volume expectations allow that
  representational error.
- Thin plate: 1 × 1 × 0.02 source units; meshing may report poor element quality.
- Rejected: disconnected shells, open edge, third incident triangle, inward or
  inconsistent winding, zero-area triangle, malformed/truncated/count-overflow data,
  self-intersection, pinched vertex fans, and nonfinite coordinates.

These 18 fixtures supplement the original 50-case CAD corpus in `../corpus-v1.json`.
The production parser, mesh/solve, convergence, and workflow harnesses exercise the
accepted M28 contract. The M28 feasibility harness deliberately omits the two new
intersection/vertex-link cases: its original parser remains a topology screen.
`stl-resource-tests.html` generates exact/over-limit data in memory and tests full
validation, fresh-worker reconstruction, cancellation, timeout, and recovery.
M29 owner acceptance remains a separate gate.
